pairs.question: Repudietur ergo misericordia?
pairs.derivation: Augustine poses a direct interrogative ('should mercy then be rejected?') and answers himself immediately with the single word 'nequaquam' ('by no means'). The answer window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('ergo amentur dolores aliquando, sed cave immunditiam...') turns from answering to exhortation, so it is cut. The preceding context is the chain of rhetorical questions about why sorrows are loved; this question/answer stands self-contained.
